title: ThinDeliveryContract
description: Validates the immutable, host-neutral authority for one opt-in thin delivery slice.

citedSkills.description: Every nw-* skill name the architecture brief cited by name (Row 13, K4 run 18) -- a mechanical carry of the citation itself, never a claim that the skill's guidance was followed. Absent or empty means the brief cited none.

droppedCitations.description: Every citation the compiler could NOT ground into a target, each with the reason it was dropped (GDP-6, reviewer counterexample 2026-08-20: an orphan bare-name citation silently vanished from the skeleton). A discarded citation stays visible to ATD/human review. Absent means nothing was dropped.

pbtAdapterResolution.description: Present only when cited-skills names the nw-property-based-testing family or a specific nw-pbt-<lang> variant (Row 13 follow-up, 2026-08-20). The variant is resolved mechanically from this contract's own target file extensions, never from the citation's own claimed language, never a silent Python default. When no installed language-specific adapter applies, this degrades to the generic nw-property-based-testing family skill (family-fallback) rather than refusing -- language specificity is an upgrade when available, never a requirement.

repositoryRelativePath.description: One repository-relative file path. Every segment is a plain name, with ONE named exception: '@v' is admitted as a whole DIRECTORY segment, the Go module-proxy convention (<module>/@v/<version>.info|.mod|.zip, <module>/@v/list) -- SF blocker 2026-08-23, where eight proxy-convention artifacts could not be declared as targets at all. Deliberately the strictest relaxation that unblocks that convention: '@' is never a free character inside a segment, '@v' is never the terminal file part, and the leading no-traversal lookahead is unchanged.

oracleLocator.description: One acceptance-oracle IDENTITY: a repository-relative file path, optionally suffixed with a '::Selector' identifier chain binding a specific test by name (Go's x_test.go::TestName, pytest's test_x.py::TestClass::test_name) -- the exact string the r2g compiler emits verbatim from a cited 'Oracle target locator:'. Consumers resolving the oracle ON DISK use only the file part (des.domain.verification_command_resolver.oracle_file_part); the selector is identity, never a path segment.

executableIdentity.description: Command = product(ExecutableIdentity, Arguments). A repository executable resolves against repository.worktree; a toolchain executable intentionally resolves through the consumer host toolchain -- this schema declares provenance only, never binary/version identity.

command.description: One verification command: a tagged executable identity paired with a literal arguments array -- never a raw argv vector or a shell string. Execution projects it to exactly [path-or-name, *arguments], with no shell and no reparsing.

supporting-locators.description: Lexicographically ordered whole-file locators whose identities and bytes join the primary acceptance oracle in delivery-closure/v2. The canonical schema validator enforces the 1.3/absent and 1.4/present version pair plus ordering; JSON Schema establishes non-empty unique repository-relative whole-file shape.

literalScriptBlock.description: One verbatim verification script carried BY-REFERENCE from the owning authority document (SF friction 2026-08-21, verification-authority delegation): 'locator' names '<repo-relative-doc>#<heading-anchor>', 'lines' are the first fenced block after that heading verbatim (an authority SCRIPT -- assignments, command substitution, negations, pipes -- never parsed into argv here), and 'content-digest' is sha256 over the lines joined with '\n' (UTF-8, no trailing newline) so the consumer verifies fidelity against the owner before faithful execution.

verificationScope.description: Exactly ONE of two forms: argv-shaped 'commands' (from a 'Verification command:' label or the subject CLAUDE.md whole-suite convention), or one 'literal-script-block' resolved from a 'Verification authority locator:' delegation -- the delegation outranks both argv sources and is never merged with them.
